text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank's Banking Department assets and liabilities stood at 3.56 trillion levs on August 1, one month after the introduction of the currency board, department's monthly balance sheet figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's Gross Domestic Product is seen rising by 2.5 to four percent this year, the Agency for Economic Analysis and Forecasts head Mariela Nenova said. @
-- Bulgaria's broad money rose by 312 billion levs to 5,335.5 billion levs in the last week of July, Bulgarian National Bank figures showed.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank's Issue Department assets and liabilities rose to 3.461 billion marks from 3.117 billion marks in the last wek of July, central bank figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov said he may sign into a law on Monday a bill for opening secret police files from the communist era approved by parliament last week. @

-- Bulgaria's Prime minister Ivan Kostov said he expected economic revival and growth in the spring but warned that the winter will be tough for a lot of Bulgarians because of the restrictions of the currency board system.
-- Bulgaria's university student Emilia Gateva spent 50 days in a cave 105 metres below earth surface in a bid to study changes in the human female organism caused by isolation under the earth.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to start this week talks with Russia's Gazprom to negotiate deliveries of Russian natural gas to Bulgaria, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to lift restrictions on the maximum level pensions in the country, effective January 1, 1998, National Social Insurance Institute head Nikolai Nikolov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
